question: Does the name recorded for the member labeled focus describe what the visible body of that section does? Judge the name against the visible behavior only. A generic or imprecise name that fits the behavior is not a mismatch.

criteria.name_mismatch: The name describes a different operation or domain than the visible body performs.
criteria.name_fits: The name is consistent with what the visible body does, even if generic or imprecise.
criteria.insufficient: The visible body is too partial or opaque to judge the name.

independentTest.corpus: none: no real-code sample has been reviewed for this question
independentTest.note: No random sample of real above-cut items has been reviewed, by an LLM or a person. The only evidence is the constructed contrast (constructedContrast).

constructedContrast.units: 50 functions renamed to another function's name against the same 50 untouched, from four public repositories
constructedContrast.note: Constructed positives are easier than real mismatches: this shows Jev registers a planted mismatch, not how often real names are wrong. One run, one day.
